Lessons.Title: Exponents That Are Unit Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Explain how to match expressions involving exponents with equivalent expressions. Justify the equivalence of $b^{1/n}$ and $\sqrt[n]{b}$ using the properties of exponents.
b^(1/n) equals its nth root where a real root is defined; for positive b the exponent identity holds without ambiguity.

Practice Problem 1: Complete the table. Use powers of 64 in the top row and radicals or rational numbers in the bottom row. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: Suppose that a friend missed class and never learned what \(25^{\frac12}\) means. Use exponent rules your friend would already know to calculate \(25^{\frac12} \boldcdot 25^{\frac12}\). Explain why this means that \(25^{\frac12}=5\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 3: Which expression is equivalent to \(16^{\frac12}\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Select all the expressions equivalent to \(4^{10}\). \(2^5 \boldcdot 2^2\) \(4^4 \boldcdot 4^6\) \(4^7 \boldcdot 4^{\text- 3}\) \(\frac{4^4}{4^{\text-6}}\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: The table shows the edge length and volume of several different cubes. Complete the table using exact values. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 6: A square has side length \(\sqrt{82}\) cm. What is the area of the square? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
